meta.mission: 6-month aesthetic body (X-frame) — body recomposition for a 25 y/o skinny-fat beginner, Delhi NCR
meta.split: Mon Lower A / Tue Push / Wed Pull / Thu Legs+Abs / Fri Upper B / Sat-Sun Rest + walking
meta.language: Simple, clear English (easy for anyone to understand)

profile.name: Athlete (Delhi NCR)
profile.experience: Beginner (did ~20 days of normal exercise before, then a gap — now a fresh restart)
profile.goal: Body recomposition / lean gain — build muscle + reduce side belly. In 5–6 months, an aesthetic X-frame body (wide shoulders + wide lats + tight waist + full legs). Slight calorie surplus, NO crash diet.
profile.diet: Non-veg (4 eggs/day, chicken on Sundays). One month is pure veg (religious).
profile.smoking: For ~5 years; wants to quit/cut down
profile.digestion: Fine with fiber; bloating without fiber (papaya, curd, water help)
profile.supplementsOwned: Creatine monohydrate + Whey 1 kg (25 g protein/scoop)

expectation.honestTruth: You won't become an Instagram model in 6 months — that takes 1.5–2 years. But if you train for 6 months without missing a single week, you'll get this:
results: Chest, shoulders, arms visibly fuller — T-shirts will start to fit well
From month 3–4, people will start asking: 'Do you go to the gym?'
expectation.core: The real test is not of the body, it's of consistency. The 20-days-on / 1-week-off game stops this time.
expectation.fiveDayConditions: The 5-day plan only works when: (1) at least 7 hours of sleep, (2) full food, (3) cigarettes down. Without these three, 4 consistent days are better than 5 half-done days.
expectation.spotReductionTruth: Spot reduction is a myth — love handles don't go from side bends or 500 crunches. Fat leaves the whole body: calorie balance + protein + patience. You train the core for strength; when fat drops, abs show. Do NOT do heavy weighted side bends — thick obliques can make the waist look wider.

trainingRules: Every session's opening (10 min, part of the plan): 5 min incline walk/cycle (until you're a little out of breath) + that day's dynamic warm-up (~5 min) + 1–2 light ramp-up sets of the first exercise.
Rest: 2–3 min on compound lifts (squat, RDL, bench, overhead press, rows, pulldown); 60–90 sec on isolation (curls, raises, pushdowns, calves, abs).
Tempo: lower the weight with 2 seconds of control, lift up with power. Don't give gravity a free ride.
How much weight? One where the last 2 reps are hard but your form doesn't break.

PROGRESSIVE OVERLOAD (the engine of growth): when all three sets hit the top of the rep range with clean form → add +2.5 kg next session. If you don't do this, the body will look the same even after 6 months.
For the first 2 weeks keep the weight light and form solid. Record your sets on your phone (side angle) — the camera doesn't lie.
Session total 60–75 min (7:00–8:15 PM). Gym closed Sat–Sun: full rest + walking.
8,000–10,000 steps daily (office + a 15 min walk after dinner — both for digestion and as a cigarette replacement).
Creatine 3–5 g EVERY day — rest days too.
Sleep: in bed by 11–11:30, at least 7 hours. Muscle BREAKS in the gym and is BUILT in sleep.
NEVER MISS TWICE: missed one day — fine, but the next day for sure. Even if you don't feel like it, go — even 30 min is enough.
universalFormRules: Spine neutral — not rounded, not over-arched. Rule #1 of every lift.
Home position for the shoulder blades — in pressing, squeeze them back-and-down; in pulling, they open first, then squeeze.
Core braced — before every rep, tighten as if you're about to take a punch to the stomach.
Full range of motion — half a rep = half the muscle.
Control — 2 seconds down, up with power.
stretchingRules: GOLDEN RULE: BEFORE exercise = dynamic (moving stretches). AFTER exercise = static (hold for 20–30 sec). Doing static first makes the muscle loose — strength drops 5–10%.
Never bounce — a jerky stretch invites a small tear. Hold it and become a statue.
Feel a stretch, not pain — a pull up to 6/10 is fine, beyond that it backfires.
Keep breathing — go a little deeper on the exhale. Hold your breath and the muscle stiffens up.
Never force a static stretch on a cold muscle — that's why static comes AFTER the workout.

weekendRoutine.satSun: Gym closed — full rest. 10 min full-body stretch at home (all of Monday's static stretches + doorway chest + child's pose). Half the soreness, fresh legs on Monday.
weekendRoutine.daily: Anytime during the day: hip flexor lunge stretch + doorway chest stretch — the daily cure for a desk job's two biggest enemies.
weekendRoutine.steps: Keep 8–10k steps going on Sat–Sun too, and keep creatine going.

crowdDodgeRules: Shuffling the order is allowed — within the SAME day you can move exercises around (bench busy? do fly/lateral first, the bench frees up in 10 min). Just don't pick up another DAY's muscle.

Keep a backup ready: Barbell bench busy → DB bench or machine chest press. Squat rack busy → goblet squat or leg press first. Lat pulldown busy → assisted pull-up or one-arm row first. Cable busy → do the same job with DBs.
Learn the magic line: 'How many sets left? Can I work in with you?' — your set during his rest, his during yours. The oldest gym trick.
muscleAudit: Upper chest — Tue (Incline DB Press)
Mid chest — Fri (Barbell Bench) + Tue fly/pec deck
Lats — 2× (Wed pull-up/pulldown + one-arm row; Fri lat pulldown)
Mid-back (rhomboids, mid traps) — 2× (Wed chest-supported row; Fri cable row)
Lower back (spinal erectors) — Mon (RDL)
Front delts — 2× (Tue + Fri presses)
Side delts — 2× direct (Tue cable lateral, Fri DB lateral) + 2 press days
Rear delts — 2× (Wed face pull; Fri reverse pec deck)
Upper traps — Wed (DB shrug) + Thu (farmer's carry)
Biceps — 2× (Wed EZ curl; Fri DB curl) + all pulls
Brachialis — Wed (hammer curl)
Triceps long head — Tue (overhead extension); lateral head — Tue + Fri (pushdowns)
Forearms — 2× (Wed hammer curl; Thu farmer's carry)
Quads — 2× (Mon squat/leg press; Thu leg press/lunges/extension)
Hamstrings — 2× (Mon RDL/lying curl; Thu seated curl)
Glutes — 3× touch (squat, RDL, lunges, leg press, bridge)
Calves: Gastrocnemius — Mon (standing raise); Soleus — Thu (seated raise)
Upper abs — Thu (cable crunch); Lower abs — Thu (hanging knee raise)
Obliques — Mon (side plank)
Rotator cuff — Wed (face pull) + band pull-aparts daily
RECOVERY CHECK: Legs Mon→Thu = 72 hrs. Chest Tue→Fri = 72 hrs. Back Wed→Fri = 48 hrs (different exercises). No muscle two days in a row. From head to toe, not a single muscle is left unworked.

week.title: LOWER A
week.crowdNote: Everyone's on the bench (International Chest Day) → the squat rack and leg section are empty — you're the king.

warmup.name: Leg swings (front-to-back)
warmup.why: Wakes up the hamstrings + hip flexors — ready for RDL.

warmup.name: Leg swings (side-to-side)
warmup.why: Opens the groin/adductors — to keep the knees out during the squat.

warmup.name: Hip circles / 90-90 rotation
warmup.why: Full rotation of the hip joint.

warmup.name: Bodyweight squats
warmup.why: Rehearsal of the squat pattern — knees-hips in sync.

warmup.name: Ankle rocks (knee-to-wall)
warmup.why: Ankle mobility — the real lock on squat depth; the heels-lifting problem gets fixed here.

warmup.name: Glute bridge
warmup.why: Switch ON the glutes that a desk job put to sleep — otherwise only the quads take over in the squat.

warmup.name: Cat-cow
warmup.why: Wake up the spine for RDL.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.form: Bar on the upper traps, chest up, back straight. Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out, heels on the floor, knees tracking over the toes. Depth: hip crease level with the knee or slightly below. (Do Goblet Squats until your form is dialed in.)
exercises.mistakes: Half-squats with ego weight; knees caving in; heels lifting.
exercises.backup: Goblet Squat or Leg Press first (if the rack is busy)

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
exercises.form: Knees soft, push the hips BACK, bar glued to the body, back completely FLAT (like a plank). Feel the stretch in the hamstrings → then back up.
exercises.mistakes: Rounding the back — this mistake is NOT forgiven. If your back looks rounded in a photo/video, that's the wrong version.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.form: Lower with full control; don't lock out the knees at the top.
exercises.mistakes: Going so low that the lower back lifts off the seat; locking the knees.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.form: Keep the hips pressed to the pad, curl with control.
exercises.mistakes: Jerking and lifting the hips.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.form: Pause 1 sec at the top, FULL stretch at the bottom. Calves are a stubborn muscle — that's why 4 sets.
exercises.mistakes: Bouncing.

exercises.name: Plank + Side Plank
exercises.form: A straight rod-like line from head to heels, squeeze the glutes, hips neither sagging nor rising. Side plank: elbow directly under the shoulder. The side plank tightens the obliques WITHOUT thickening them — that's why no weighted side bends (they widen the waist and ruin the X-frame).
exercises.mistakes: Hips sagging or rising up.

static.name: Standing quad stretch
static.target: Quads — pull the heel toward the hip.

static.name: Hamstring stretch
static.target: Hamstrings — leg straight, hinge forward from the hips.

static.name: Figure-4 / Pigeon
static.target: Glutes.

static.name: Butterfly
static.target: Groin/adductors.

static.name: Wall calf stretch (straight leg)
static.target: Gastrocnemius.

static.name: Hip flexor lunge stretch
static.target: Hip flexors — knee on the floor, push the hips forward. The tightest muscle from a desk job; do it at home daily too.

static.name: Child's pose
static.target: Lower-back release — while breathing out.

week.title: PUSH (Chest, Shoulders, Triceps)
week.crowdNote: Monday's chest crowd is on back today → incline bench, pec deck, shoulder press all free.

warmup.name: Arm circles
warmup.why: Warmth into the shoulder joint.

warmup.name: Shoulder dislocates (towel/band/rod)
warmup.why: Opens all angles of the shoulder, and stretches the chest too. Don't be scared of the name.

warmup.name: Band pull-aparts
warmup.why: Rear delts + rotator cuff ON — shoulder insurance before pressing.

warmup.name: Wall slides
warmup.why: Smooth movement of the shoulder blades (scapula).

warmup.name: Open-close hugs (arm swings)
warmup.why: A dynamic stretch for the chest.

warmup.name: Push-ups
warmup.why: Rehearsal of today's pressing pattern.

warmup.name: Wrist circles + light wrist stretch
warmup.why: All the pressing load passes through the wrist.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.form: Bench ~30°, forearms always vertical, bring the dumbbells together over the chest (don't clang them), lower with control. This is what builds an aesthetic chest — a flat bench doesn't fully fill the upper part.
exercises.mistakes: Setting the bench to 45°+ — then the shoulder takes over more and the chest less.

exercises.name: Pec Deck / Cable Fly
exercises.form: Elbows slightly bent and FIXED, bring the arms together like a hug.
exercises.mistakes: Going heavy and changing the elbow angle.

exercises.name: Seated Overhead Press (barbell/machine)
exercises.form: Core tight, ribs down, no over-arching of the lower back, press all the way up.
exercises.mistakes: Going heavy and doing half reps.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.form: This muscle is the width of the X-frame. Lead with the elbows, up to shoulder height, keep the slight elbow bend the SAME through the whole rep. Cable = constant tension.
exercises.mistakes: Swinging; shrugging the traps.

exercises.name: Overhead DB Triceps Extension
exercises.form: The long head is the biggest part of the arm and it only gets a full stretch in the overhead position. Elbows near the ears, only the forearms move.
exercises.mistakes: Elbows flaring out; the elbows moving around.

exercises.name: Rope Pushdown
exercises.form: Elbows fixed to the body, full lockout squeeze at the bottom, spread the rope ends apart at the bottom.
exercises.mistakes: Leaning the shoulders forward and using body weight.

static.name: Doorway chest stretch
static.target: Pecs — hand on the doorframe, lean forward.

static.name: Overhead triceps stretch
static.target: Triceps long head — elbow up, hand behind.

static.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
static.target: Side + rear delt.

static.name: Hands-behind-back chest opener
static.target: Front delts + chest — interlock the hands behind and open the chest.

static.name: Neck side stretch
static.target: Traps — ear toward the shoulder (traps get tight during pressing).

week.title: PULL (Back, Rear Delts, Biceps)
week.crowdNote: Today is the bros' shoulder day → lat pulldown, rows, pull-up station empty.

warmup.name: Arm circles + shoulder rolls
warmup.why: Shoulders warm.

warmup.name: Band pull-aparts
warmup.why: A daily ritual — the rear delt should never go cold.

warmup.name: Cat-cow + T-spine rotation (open book)
warmup.why: Upper-spine rotation is needed for rowing.

warmup.name: Dead hang
warmup.why: Lat stretch + spine decompression + grip warm-up — the perfect starter for pull day.

warmup.name: Scapular pulls
warmup.why: In a dead hang, pull the shoulders down without bending the elbows — it teaches you to switch the lats ON; the first step to a pull-up.

warmup.name: Wrist/forearm circles
warmup.why: For curls + grip.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-up / Close-grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.form: Reduce the assist weight a little each week. Target: your first unassisted pull-up in month 3.
exercises.mistakes: Half range; jerking.

exercises.name: Chest-supported Row
exercises.form: Chest on the pad — cheating is impossible, best for a beginner. Pull the elbows back, 1 sec squeeze. (Barbell Row option: back flat, no jerking.)
exercises.mistakes: Jerking the whole body (rounding the back in the barbell version).

exercises.name: One-arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.form: One hand and knee on the bench, back FLAT like a table, pull the elbow toward the hip, keep the torso square.
exercises.mistakes: Rotating the torso; jerking.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.form: The hidden hero: 3D shoulders are built from behind + it repairs the hunched-forward desk-job posture + shoulder injury insurance. Rope at eye level, elbows HIGH (above the shoulders), pull the ends apart, finish like a 'double biceps pose'.
exercises.mistakes: Going heavy and turning it into a row. 90% of people get this wrong.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.form: The muscle on the side of the neck that shows above the collar. Shoulders straight UP, 1 sec hold at the top, lower with control.
exercises.mistakes: Rolling the shoulders in circles — useless and risky.

exercises.name: EZ-bar Curl
exercises.form: Elbows FIXED to the body, full range — full stretch at the bottom, squeeze at the top.
exercises.mistakes: Swinging from the lower back.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.form: Neutral grip (palms facing each other), elbows steady, with control.
exercises.mistakes: Swinging with the body.

static.name: Lat stretch (holding the rack)
static.target: Lats — hold the rack, hips back, lean to the side. The KING stretch of pull day.

static.name: Biceps wall stretch
static.target: Biceps — palm on the wall behind you, turn the body forward.

static.name: Forearm stretches (both)
static.target: Forearms — palm up and pull the fingers back, then palm down. A must after hammer curls.

static.name: Upper trap stretch
static.target: Upper traps — ear toward the shoulder, light pressure with the hand. After shrugs.

static.name: Cross-body rear delt stretch
static.target: Rear delts.

static.name: Child's pose side reach
static.target: A second angle for the lats — reaching the arm to one side.

week.title: LEGS + ABS
week.crowdNote: Today everyone's hitting arms, there's a line at the cable for curls/pushdowns → the leg area is totally deserted.

warmup.name: Leg swings (both directions)
warmup.why: Hips + hamstrings ready.

warmup.name: Bodyweight squats
warmup.why: Pattern on.

warmup.name: Reverse lunges
warmup.why: Today is walking lunges — groove the pattern first without weight.

warmup.name: Hip circles + ankle rocks
warmup.why: Hips + ankles opened up.

warmup.name: Glute bridge
warmup.why: Glutes ON.

warmup.name: Dead hang
warmup.why: Grip + shoulders ready for hanging knee raises.

warmup.name: Standing torso twists
warmup.why: Wake up the core/spine for the crunch work.

exercises.name: Leg Press (Heavy Day)
exercises.form: A little more weight than Monday, exactly the same form. Lower with control, don't lock the knees.
exercises.mistakes: Cutting the range short for the sake of weight.

exercises.name: Walking Lunges
secondary: Core + small hip stabilizers (balance, athletic look)
exercises.form: Both knees at 90°, front knee OVER the foot (not past it), torso upright, back knee just touching the floor.
exercises.mistakes: Small steps; leaning forward.
exercises.backup: Reverse Lunges (if you have a balance issue)

exercises.name: Leg Extension
primary: Quads (isolate — vastus medialis/teardrop, above the knee)
exercises.form: 1 sec squeeze at the top, lower with control.
exercises.mistakes: Kicking with a jerk.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.form: The seated angle gives a different stretch than lying — Monday was lying, today is seated. Curl with control.
exercises.mistakes: Half range.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
primary: Soleus (the lower calf muscle — only worked with a bent knee)
exercises.form: Monday standing = gastro, today seated = soleus. Calf complete. 1 sec at the top, full stretch at the bottom.
exercises.mistakes: Bounce.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
primary: Lower abs (the lower part of the rectus abdominis)
exercises.form: Curl the pelvis UP — don't just swing the legs.
exercises.mistakes: Counting reps from swinging.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.form: Hips FIXED, crunch down by only rounding the spine. Abs are a muscle too — they grow with weight, not just floor crunches.
exercises.mistakes: Bending from the hips (not rounding the spine).
exercises.backup: Decline bench crunch (if the cable is busy — same upper abs)

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.form: Heavy DBs in both hands, walk tall and straight — shoulders back, core tight.
exercises.mistakes: Walking hunched over. (If there's no space: stand and hold heavy DBs for 30–40 sec — same job.)

static.name: Quad + Hip flexor lunge stretch
static.target: After lunges, both of these are NON-NEGOTIABLE.

static.name: Hamstring stretch
static.target: Hamstrings.

static.name: Figure-4 glute stretch
static.target: Glutes.

static.name: Calf stretch (both versions)
static.target: Straight leg = gastro; slightly bent knee = soleus (today's seated calf was for this).

static.name: Cobra stretch
static.target: An ab stretch — lengthen the stomach muscles after crunches, a reverse bend for the spine.

static.name: Child's pose
static.target: The signature move to finish.

week.title: UPPER B
week.crowdNote: On Friday half the people do legs and half don't even come → bench and machines are free.

warmup.name: Arm circles
warmup.why: Shoulders warm.

warmup.name: Shoulder dislocates
warmup.why: All angles opened up.

warmup.name: Band pull-aparts
warmup.why: Rear delt + cuff ON.

warmup.name: Wall slides
warmup.why: Scapula smooth.

warmup.name: Push-ups
warmup.why: Rehearsal for the bench.

warmup.name: Dead hang + scapular pulls
warmup.why: Pulldown-row ready.

warmup.name: Cat-cow + wrist circles
warmup.why: Spine + wrists ready.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.form: Tuesday incline = upper chest, today flat = mid chest → chest COMPLETE. 5-point contact: head + upper back + hips on the bench, both feet planted on the floor. Squeeze the shoulder blades back, slight natural arch, bar touches mid-chest, elbows ~45°.
exercises.mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest; lifting the hips off the bench; flaring the elbows to 90° (risky for the shoulder).
exercises.backup: DB Bench or Machine Chest Press (if the bench is busy)

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.form: Chest up, slight lean back (10–15°, more than that = cheating), bar to the collarbone, elbows down-and-back, shoulders pressed DOWN (no shrugging).
exercises.mistakes: Pulling with momentum by swinging back.
exercises.backup: Assisted Pull-up or One-arm Row first

exercises.name: Seated DB Shoulder Press
exercises.form: Tuesday was barbell/machine, today is DB — the stabilizers work too. Core tight, lower back straight, full press.
exercises.mistakes: Over-arch; half reps.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.form: Pull the elbows toward your waist, 1 sec squeeze, chest up.
exercises.mistakes: Jerking and rocking the whole body back and forth.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.form: Light and clean. Keep the elbow bend fixed, wrist not below the elbow, up to shoulder height — dumbbell and elbow roughly in one line.
exercises.mistakes: Going heavy and swinging; shrugging the traps.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.form: Big shoulder from the front, flat from the back — no more of that incomplete look. Open the arms and squeeze back, keep the weight light.
exercises.mistakes: Going heavy and turning it into a row.

exercises.name: Superset: DB Curl + Rope Pushdown
exercises.form: The week's arm finisher — head into the weekend with a pump. Curl: elbows glued to the body, no swinging. Pushdown: elbows fixed, full lockout squeeze at the bottom.
exercises.mistakes: Breaking form in a rush.

static.name: Doorway chest stretch
static.target: Pecs.

static.name: Lat stretch (on the rack)
static.target: Lats.

static.name: Cross-body shoulder + rear delt stretch
static.target: Side + rear delts.

static.name: Overhead triceps stretch
static.target: Triceps.

static.name: Biceps wall stretch
static.target: Biceps.

static.name: Forearm stretches (both)
static.target: Forearms.

static.name: Neck/trap stretch + deep breath
static.target: Traps — week done. A full upper-body service complete before the weekend.

regular.label: Regular (Non-veg)
regular.targets: ~2,500–2,600 kcal (slight surplus — not a bulk) | Protein 110–120 g/day | Water 3–4 L

meals.food: Home food — lentils + rice/flatbread + vegetables + 1 bowl curd
1 banana + a handful of peanuts or peanut-butter bread
Soya chunks 60 g dry (in a curry/pilaf). Sunday + one weekday: chicken 250 g. With flatbread/rice + salad + papaya

regular.note: This gives ~100–110 g protein without whey. Keep the fiber system going daily: papaya, curd, salad, water — your stomach has already told you what it needs.

budget.item: Left over ~Rs.1,200: unflavoured whey concentrate 1 kg on sale, otherwise extra eggs/soya

regular.priority: Priority always: food first, then creatine, then whey. Whey is convenience, not magic.

veg.label: Veg Month
veg.targets: ~2,500 kcal | Protein ~115–125 g/day | Water 3–4 L (more lentils-soya, so water is even more important or you'll bloat)

meals.food: Lentils 2 bowls + flatbread/rice + vegetables + curd 1 bowl
1 banana + a handful of peanuts, or a sattu shake (30 g sattu + water + lemon)
Soya chunks 50 g dry (in a curry/pilaf) + 2 flatbreads + salad + papaya

veg.note: You easily cross 100 g — there's a buffer too. If eggs are allowed, tell me and it gets even easier. If paneer is expensive, do 100 g on alternate days instead of daily + soya 75 g on the other days — protein stays the same.

budget.item: Paneer (3 kg — loose from a local dairy, cheaper than packaged)
Curd (or set it at home from milk — almost free)
Whey + creatine already in hand — this month the budget fits easily

veg.priority: In the veg month creatine is EVEN MORE important — natural creatine comes from meat; veg people benefit the most from the supplement. The timing is perfect.

supplements.name: Creatine monohydrate
supplements.detail: 3–5 g EVERY DAY (rest days too), any time, with water — drink plenty of water. The most research-backed supplement; you'll see a difference in both strength and size.

supplements.name: Whey (25 g protein/scoop)
supplements.detail: 1 scoop post-workout in 250 ml milk. A 1 kg pack lasts almost the whole month. You can take it on rest days too if your food falls short.

supplementsPriority: Priority order: food first, then creatine, then whey.

lifestyle.cardio: 8,000–10,000 steps daily (office walking + 15 min after dinner). Sat: option of a brisk/incline walk. Spot reduction is a myth — fat leaves through calorie balance, walking supports that + improves digestion.
lifestyle.sleep: In bed by 11–11:30, at least 7 hours. Muscle breaks in the gym and is built in sleep.
smoking: Cigarettes are robbing your oxygen and recovery — stamina down, pump down, recovery slow. Deciding to quit is the best decision for your profile.
First target: replace the after-meal and after-gym cigarette with a 10-min walk.
Cut the count in HALF this month. On 5-day training, the cigarette tax is doubled.
A 35-year pattern: as you get stronger in the gym, the cigarette weakens on its own.

tracking.start: Day 1: take a photo (front + side), keep the same lighting going forward.
tracking.biweekly: Every 2 weeks: waist tape at the navel + weight in the morning on an empty stomach.
tracking.perfectRecomp: Weight stable or +0.5 kg/month max, waist the same or dropping.
tracking.adjust: If the belly grows, cut flatbread/rice a little. If weight doesn't move for 4+ weeks, increase food a little.
tracking.sundayReport: Sunday night: the week's report — whichever exercise you had form doubts on gets polished first.
tracking.mindset: NEVER MISS TWICE. Missed one day — the next day for sure, even 30 min is fine.

references.muscleWiki: MuscleWiki: musclewiki.com — a body diagram; click a muscle → all exercises for that muscle with videos + primary/secondary muscles listed. There's an app too. Every exercise's photo + video + diagram in one place, free.
references.youtube: YouTube: the 'Video' link on each exercise opens a YouTube search — watch any 1-min technique video from the top results. Search pattern: '[exercise name] proper form'.
references.camera: Camera: the biggest pro move — record your set on your phone (side angle) and compare it to a reference. The mirror lies, the camera doesn't.
references.charts: Charts: print a dynamic warm-up chart + a full-body stretching chart (e.g. DAREBEE's free charts) and keep them in your gym bag.

closing: Now the thinking part is done — only the doing part is left. Never miss twice. — Coach
